history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. It's completely dead as far as the network goes.

I can help you troubleshoot this issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, customer ID, or your full name and date of birth? This will help me check your line status and assist you further.

Thank you for providing your phone number. Your line status is currently listed as Active, which means there are no suspensions or contract issues on our end.

To help you further, I’ll need you to perform a few quick checks on your device. Are you able to check your phone’s status bar and SIM card status? This will help us determine if the issue is with your device settings or the network. If you need instructions, let me know!
Sure, I can check those for you. Where would you like me to start—the status bar or the SIM card status?

Let’s start by checking your phone’s status bar. Please look at the top of your phone’s screen and let me know:

- If you see any icons like Airplane Mode (✈️), “No Signal” (📵), or any signal bars (📶).
- If there are any network type indicators (like 5G, 4G, LTE, etc.).
- If mobile data is enabled or disabled.

Once you provide this information, we’ll move on to checking your SIM card status if needed.
At the top of my screen, I see the Airplane Mode icon, 'No Signal,' and it says data is enabled. There are no signal bars or network indicators.

It looks like Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless connections—including cellular service—are turned off, which explains why you have no signal or network access.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your device. Once you do, check if your signal bars return and if you can use your phone normally. Let me know what you see after turning off Airplane Mode.
Airplane mode is now off, but I still don't see any signal bars or network indicators—just 'No Signal.' The problem hasn't changed.

Thank you for checking. Since Airplane Mode is now off but you still see “No Signal,” the next step is to check your SIM card status. This will help us determine if your phone is detecting the SIM card properly.

Please check your SIM card status in your phone’s settings and let me know if it shows as:
- Active/Ready
- Missing/Not detected
- Locked (PIN or PUK required)

Let me know what your phone reports for the SIM card status.
My SIM card status shows as active. So, the phone is detecting the SIM card, but I still have no signal or network connection.

Thank you for confirming that your SIM card is active. Since your SIM is detected and Airplane Mode is off, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to the network.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if the MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL is missing. If you’re unsure, just let me know what you see, and I can guide you further.
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is 'fast.telecom.net', but the status says 'Not set'. The MMSC URL is listed as 'http://mms.telecom.net/mms/wapenc'.

Thank you for providing the APN details. The APN name showing as “Not set” (despite having a value) could indicate a configuration issue that may prevent your phone from connecting to the network.

Let’s try resetting your APN settings to the default values. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Please reset your APN settings now. Once you’ve done that, restart your phone and let me know if you see any signal bars or network indicators after the reboot.

I reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone. The APN is now set to 'internet' with the MMSC URL 'http://mms.carrier.com/mms'. After rebooting, I still see 'No Signal' at the top—no bars or network indicators.

Thank you for following those steps. Since your SIM card is active, Airplane Mode is off, and your APN settings have been reset, but you still see “No Signal,” this suggests a deeper network or device issue.

Before escalating, let’s try one more step: reseating your SIM card. Please remove your SIM card from your phone, wait a few seconds, and then reinsert it securely. After reinserting, check if your phone detects any signal or network connection.

Let me know the result after you reseat your SIM card.
I removed and reinserted the SIM card. My phone still shows 'No Signal' at the top—no bars or network indicators. The SIM status is active.

Thank you for trying all the troubleshooting steps. Since your SIM card is active, Airplane Mode is off, APN settings are correct, and reseating the SIM did not resolve the issue, this may indicate a more complex network or device problem that requires advanced support.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can assist you further with this issue.

YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
